patterns.name: Help listing treated as the accepted-value set
patterns.example: The executor reported that --permission-mode has no 'default' value because help lists only manual; the parent probe showed both spellings exit 0 and system/init reports default.

patterns.name: Startup permission mode can be ambient and is not pinned by --safe-mode
patterns.example: A --safe-mode dispatch with no --permission-mode reported permissionMode: "auto" in system/init and auto-approved an edit on sonnet; an explicit --permission-mode default denied the same edit. The unflagged (no --safe-mode) run reported default.
patterns.generalFixRule: Never rely on the startup default: pass --permission-mode explicitly on every dispatch and resume, and read system/init.permissionMode as the effective mode; treat a mode that is not the chosen one as a setup anomaly.
patterns.fix: v6: the read-only and implementation bullets require an explicit --permission-mode (default/Manual for read-only, acceptEdits for implementation); Verify now requires confirming permissionMode from system/init; constraints.md and cli-contract.md carry the observed evidence; validation.json records probes p17-p19.
patterns.fixStatus: resolved in iter7 (all three runs pinned --permission-mode explicitly; iter7-B noted the ambient auto default and that pinning prevented it)

patterns.name: Load-boundary verification signal undefined
patterns.example: system/init still listed 16 skills and 5 plugins under --safe-mode; the event alone does not show whether customizations were suppressed.
patterns.generalFixRule: Judge suppression from behavioral signals in the stream (empty mcp_servers, no hook events, no customization-driven actions) rather than from flag names or the advertised skill/plugin lists, and record which signals were used.
patterns.fix: v6 (partial): Verify now says to confirm the load boundary from the run's own evidence (permissionMode, model, mcp_servers). The skills/plugins nuance and 'record which signals' are not yet spelled out.
patterns.fixStatus: partially-applied-in-v6; resolved in iter7-B/C (stream-json used and mcp_servers [] recorded as the boundary signal)

patterns.fix: v6: the brief guidance scopes the rule to source and spec files when the workspace already carries runtime artifacts or the README prescribes a bytecode-writing command.

acceptedMinorObservations.name: Harness no-poll policy versus the task's bounded wait
acceptedMinorObservations.note: The dispatch wrapper asks for a capped in-session wait while the subagent harness advertises notification-based resume. Harness-attributable; the skill's own supervision rule (never duplicate on yield) was followed throughout.

acceptedMinorObservations.name: VCS detection as an explicit preflight step
acceptedMinorObservations.note: Non-blocking framing preference; the skill already defines the non-git fallback.

acceptedMinorObservations.note: Non-blocking; the skill's delta-brief contents already cover the continuation, and executors briefed the probe like a normal run.

acceptedMinorObservations.name: Preflight non-mutation validation on a copy
acceptedMinorObservations.note: Non-blocking good practice performed by several executors; the skill's scoping rule already prevents the inconsistency.

acceptedMinorObservations.name: Standalone sleep blocked by the CLI's own Bash guard
acceptedMinorObservations.note: A mandated `sleep 45` was rejected by Claude Code's tool guard even though `Bash(sleep *)` was allowlisted; the delegate relaunched it in the background. An allowlist rule is not a guarantee about how a command executes. For a controlled idle interval, use a loop shape the guard accepts or a backgrounded task the brief waits on, and confirm the wait from the stream.

acceptedMinorObservations.name: Resume emits a zero-turn stub result
acceptedMinorObservations.note: The resumed run's stream carried a stub `result` (num_turns 0, empty text) before the real result. Reading the last result event, as the skill already says, resolves it.

acceptedMinorObservations.name: Rate-limit state visible only in stream events
acceptedMinorObservations.note: Account rate windows and overage state appear in `rate_limit_event` stream events and not in plain result JSON. The skill's format-selection rule already ties the transport to the evidence the report must state.

interpretation: Self-reported friction is classified against the frozen requirements and parent verification before it becomes a fix. A documented limitation, an explicit discretionary choice, or a tool-documentation quirk is not automatically a missing instruction. Materiality bar for fix rounds: an item is actionable when it changes the run's correctness, safety, or evidence quality; wording preferences and checklist/harness artifacts are recorded without cutting a new candidate.
